newsitem.title: UK: World airport security still poor - British magazine.
newsitem.headline: World airport security still poor - British magazine.

text.p: Security at many airports around the world remains inadequate and 8,000 unaccompanied bags find their way on to international flights every day, a leading British consumer magazine said on Friday.

Despite tragedies such as the 1988 Lockerbie disaster, in which a bomb in the baggage hold of Pan Am flight 103 killed 270 people, most countries had failed to introduce legislation requiring the screening of all hold baggage on international flights, Holiday Which? magazine said.

"One of the major stumbling blocks -- other arguments include cost and flight delays -- is that there is no international body with the power to enforce security standards or carry out regular inspections," the magazine said.
Many airports had not installed the security systems needed to detect plastic explosives of the kind used in the bomb that destroyed the Pan Am jumbo jet over Lockerbie.

By September last year only four U.S. airports -- Atlanta, Atlantic City, New York's Kennedy and San Francisco -- had installed the bomb detector system approved by the U.S. airline regulatory authorities.
Many European airports screened as little as five to 10 percent of hold luggage, although for high-risk flights the proportion may be higher.

Holiday Which? editor Patricia Yates said: "We want to see governments, rather than airlines, taking responsibility for security procedures at home and abroad -- perhaps with agreement between countries."
